name: Action for Children (England example)
basis: Illustrative example only: weekly fee £700 + weekly allowance £190 = £890, for a parent and child arrangement. Fee and allowance combined (allowance covers food, clothing, toiletries, day-to-day living). Page states figures are for illustration and individual fees and allowances will vary. Not a standard single-child rate.
dependsOn: Location, type of fostering, siblings, complex needs (specialist add-on payments); 'many factors'

name: Apex Fostering
basis: Minimum £500 per week tax-free for one child (body text); the FAQ on the same page says 'a minimum of £450 per week' - the page does not reconcile the two. Can increase to £1000 per week for children with more complex needs. Page does not say whether the figure includes the child's allowance, only that pay is intended to cover the child's costs. Plus two extra weeks' payment per year for holidays. Operates in East/North London, Beds, Bucks, Cambs, Herts, Essex, Lincs, Northants, Peterborough.
dependsOn: Child's needs / level of care required; type of placement

name: Barnardo's Fostering
basis: fees and allowances combined: 'the payment you receive from us will be made up of two elements' (per-child allowance and foster carer fee); £495 is an average, £630 an upper figure
dependsOn: type of foster care, number of children, child's age, child's needs

name: Capstone Foster Care
basis: 'Total allowances' per week per arrangement; page does not split fee and allowance
dependsOn: child's needs (level of training/support required), child's age, location, type of arrangement (standard over £460; therapeutic MATTS up to £660; parent and child from £910), number of children

name: Caritas Care
basis: £405.00 to £642.00 per full week per child, paid weekly; birthday, holiday and religious festival allowances paid separately on top. Page does not state whether the figure splits into child allowance and carer fee. Allowances reviewed yearly.
dependsOn: Not stated on the page (no age, level or needs criteria given)

name: Clifford House Fostering
basis: Three carer grades, each with a range by child's age, per week per child: Grade 1 (new) £407.68-£494.62; Grade 2 (after 12 months and core training) £417.69-£503.63; Grade 3 (3+ years) £427.70-£514.64. Page says the weekly payment comprises two elements, a child allowance and a professional fee, so the figures are the combined total. Page also says 'up to £25,991 per child each year'. Agency based in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire.
dependsOn: Child's age (lower figure younger children, higher older); carer's grade/experience

name: Compass Fostering
basis: per child per week; page says 'Your fostering payment is made up of' a professional fee and a living allowance for the child; figures described as 'illustrative only'
dependsOn: number of children, child's needs, type of fostering (standard £434–£465.50 by age; therapeutic £668.50; parent and child £791), carer experience

name: Five Rivers Child Care
basis: 'a weekly foster care allowance made up of a professional fee and a living allowance for the child'; stated as 'up to', not split
dependsOn: child's age, whether siblings are also placed, additional needs (payments adjusted)

name: Foster Care Associates (FCA)
basis: per child per week; page says the allowance has two parts (expenses for the child and a professional fee) but does not label the weekly figures as the combined total
dependsOn: child's age and complexity of needs; placement type (standard child over 11 = £508.20; enhanced/complex = £549; parent and child up to £917)

name: Fostering People
basis: per child per week; meta description says carers receive 'a fostering allowance and fee for each child' but body does not split or label the figures as totals
dependsOn: child's age (standard for child over 5 in England over £521), individual needs (enhanced allowance), type of placement (mother and baby example £849.06), number of children

name: Fostering UK
basis: £400-700 per week per child depending on the type of placement. Presented as a per-child weekly allowance covering the child's care (food, clothing, activities); page does not state a fee/allowance split. Homepage describes the organisation as recruiting and supporting its own 'therapeutic foster care specialists' (Peterborough, Buckinghamshire, Milton Keynes, Luton, Watford); Ofsted registration not stated on the pages fetched, so verify it is an IFA before use.
dependsOn: Type of placement; child's age and circumstances; higher allowance for ASD, disabilities or special behavioural needs

name: Fosterplus
basis: per week; page says the weekly payment 'is split into two parts' (child allowance and professional fee) but does not label the range as the combined total
dependsOn: where you live (England or Scotland), your experience, the child in your care

name: ISP Fostering
basis: per child per week; 'the weekly fostering payment' described as two parts (cost of the child plus professional fee); tier figures are the full weekly payment
dependsOn: carer tier: Core £572.74, Main £635.46, Senior £660.52 (London: £616.70 / £685.51 / £713.16); parent and child £946.75

name: Little Acorns Fostering
basis: Standard weekly fostering allowance £440 per child; can increase up to £900 per week depending on the child's needs and placement type; parent and child placements start from £700 per week. Page says the allowance 'covers all child-related costs' but does not state a separate fee/allowance split. Agency based in Haverhill, Suffolk.
dependsOn: Child's needs; type of fostering placement (parent and child from £700)

name: Mosaic Foster Care
basis: £600 per week minimum, increasing to £700+ per week after completing training (upper figure is open-ended '£700+'). Full payment for each additional child. Page says allowances and fees 'are combined into one' payment at Mosaic. £250 per week retainer for up to 4 weeks after a placement of 6+ months ends. Offices in Southend-on-Sea and Northampton.
dependsOn: Carer's completion of training; number of children

name: National Fostering Group (NFG)
basis: average per child per week; page says fostering pay 'is made up of 2 parts' (an allowance for the child's needs and a professional fee) and the FAQ says the figure 'covers their professional fee and their foster child's needs'
dependsOn: type of fostering (standard average £487; enhanced/complex needs average £652), skills, location, number of children

name: Nexus Fostering
basis: single worked example (therapeutic carers) stated per week, tax free; page does not say whether it is allowance plus fee
dependsOn: age and needs of the child, type of fostering (therapeutic pays more), carer experience; paid per child

name: Orange Grove Foster Care
basis: per child per week; allowance described as comprising a child's allowance and a foster parent payment, figures not split or labelled as totals
dependsOn: carer grade (Grade 1 £410–£497; Grade 2 £420–£507; Grade 3 £430–£517, based on experience/training/years fostering) and child's age

name: Parallel Parents
basis: Up to £500 per week per child; page also says roughly £20,000 per annum paid weekly, with a level system adding roughly an extra £1,000 per child per annum for experience. Page does not say whether the figure includes the child's allowance.
dependsOn: Carer's experience/level (training), child's specific needs, number of children

name: Sparks Fostering
basis: Up to £750 per child per week; page says the current average is £750, for carers (qualified childcare professionals) looking after teenagers with additional needs; set at 50% of the local authority fee. Plus around £1,300 per year in additional allowances. Page says fees and allowances 'are paid together and rarely split into two payments'. Fee comparison dated October 2024; agency covers England, comparison focuses on the North West.
dependsOn: Carer's qualifications; teenagers with additional needs; linked to the local authority fee

name: Sunbeam Fostering Agency
basis: Up to £700 per child per week; ceiling only, no minimum stated. Page also gives annual indications: one child with additional needs up to £36,400 pa; parent and child up to £33,540 pa (based on 2021 payments). Page does not say whether the £700 includes the child's maintenance allowance; it describes the payment as allowance element plus reward element.
dependsOn: Child's needs (complex needs, parent and child, remand attract higher rates); each placement assessed individually

name: Swiis Foster Care (England)
basis: 'a combined allowance each week' (part for the child's costs, part a fee for the carer); all weekly figures stated as 'up to' per placement type
dependsOn: placement type and number of children (one child up to £625; enhanced one child placed alone with additional needs up to £1,380; two siblings up to £1,218; two unrelated children up to £1,250; parent and child up to £1,167), child's age, region, individual assessment

name: TACT Fostering
basis: average weekly pay per placement; Fostering Pay described as a maintenance payment plus a fee, and birthday, festival, holiday, short-break and council-tax elements 'have been prorated into the weekly pay examples'
dependsOn: child's age, complexity of needs (single child average £491; child with additional needs £564), number of children (two children £982), type of care (parent and child £817)

name: Team Fostering
basis: £554.12 per week (£28,814.25 per year) for a child aged 11 and over; rate for under-11s not stated; higher rate where a child is assessed as having additional difficulties (amount not given). Payments not reduced for additional children (two children aged 12 and 14 = £57,628.48 per year). Page refers to 'Carer Fees' and says carers cover food, clothing, transport and activities from the payment; does not explicitly state an allowance/fee split.
dependsOn: Child's age; child's assessed additional difficulties

name: Action for Children (Northern Ireland example)
basis: Illustrative example only: weekly fee £476 + weekly allowance £166 = £642 for one foster child with special needs. Fee and allowance combined. Page states individual fees and allowances will vary.
dependsOn: Location, type of fostering, siblings, complex needs; special needs shown in the example

name: Action for Children (Scotland example)
basis: Illustrative example only: weekly fee £570 + weekly allowance £199 = £769 for one foster child under 16. Fee and allowance combined. Page states individual fees and allowances will vary.
dependsOn: Location, type of fostering, siblings, complex needs; child's age shown only in the example

name: FCA Scotland
basis: per child per week, described as 'allowances'; page does not state whether the fee is included
dependsOn: child's age and complexity of needs; placement type

name: Swiis Foster Care Scotland
basis: 'a combined allowance each week' (child's costs plus carer fee); 'Swiis pays up to' table by age band: 0–4 £442; 5–10 £471; 11–15 £559; 16+ £563
dependsOn: child's age, placement type (one child up to £563; enhanced one child up to £746; two siblings up to £986; two unrelated children up to £1,126; parent and child up to £746), additional needs, region

name: Birmingham Children's Trust (Foster Birmingham)
basis: fee per child per week (Level 3 £217.28; Level 4 £294.58) plus child maintenance allowance £184.75–£292.45 per child per week by age; only the worked examples give a 'Total Weekly Payment' (£402.03 for Level 3 with one child aged 4)
dependsOn: carer level (3 or 4), child's age, number of children

name: East Sussex County Council
basis: table column 'Weekly payments total' under the heading 'Combined Fostering Maintenance Allowance and Professional Fee'

name: Foster for Greater Manchester (10 GM councils incl. Manchester)
basis: combined weekly fee and allowance per child
dependsOn: carer experience, type of fostering, child's age; each GM council sets its own rates

name: Kent County Council (Kent Fostering)
basis: weekly total per child = maintenance (allowance) plus reward (fee), by age band and fostering type
dependsOn: child's age band (under 2, 2–4, 5–8, 9–10, 11–15, 16–18) and type of fostering: standard £341.82–£574.30; solo and complex £486.56–£849.22; disabled children standard £424.30–£656.78; disabled enhanced £451.79–£684.27; parent and child up to £1,191.04

name: London Borough of Bromley
basis: per child per week total = child allowance plus carer professional fee, shown in a table with a Total column
dependsOn: child's age band (0–4 £407.66; 5–10 £431.66; 11–12 £463.66; 13–15 £515.27; 16+ £557.27); enhanced fee of £50 per week by agreement; parent and child total £823.93

name: Sheffield City Council
basis: total weekly payment per child = fostering allowance (follows the national minimum, by age) plus skill level fee, shown as a totals table
dependsOn: carer skill level (Level 1 £301–£443; Level 2 £366–£458; Level 3 £386–£468) and child's age band (0–4, 5–7, 8–10, 11–15, 16+)

name: Wigan Council
basis: weekly rate per child by carer tier and DfE age band; booklet does not explicitly state that tier rates combine allowance and skills fee (Tier 1 'maintenance payment' only = £176–£267, matching the national minimum; higher tiers exceed it)
dependsOn: carer tier (Tier 2 newly approved £296.23–£418.29; Tier 3 experienced £373.69–£518.71; Tier 4 specialist £725.18 / £812.49 / £915.01) and child's age band (0–2, 3–4, 5–10, 11–15, 16–17)

name: City of Edinburgh Council (Edinburgh Fostering)
basis: weekly payments per child; page lists a weekly fee (£307.50 for ages 0–11 and 12+; £490.06 disability and specialist) and a weekly standard allowance by age (£177.70 / £206.72 / £206.72 / £283.37); the stated range equals fee plus allowance but is not explicitly labelled as such
dependsOn: child's age and placement type (disability and specialist fee is higher)

name: Renfrewshire Council
basis: per child per week, stated as made up of a weekly fostering payment (fee) of £330.46 per child plus a weekly allowance by age (£178.56 age 0–4; £207.73 age 5–15; £284.75 age 16–17)
dependsOn: child's age (allowance); the £330.46 fee is a flat per-child amount

name: Foster Wales Swansea (Swansea Council)
basis: per week per child; page does not say whether allowance and fee are combined
dependsOn: type of fostering, number of children, length of fostering
